messages:
sam: Heads-up — noticed huge queue depth in us-east-1 around 16:20 UTC. Short interactive requests are piling up behind a few long streaming jobs; GPU utilization per node is ~35% but queue depth is 580. Logs show many jobs sitting in QUEUED for 2+ minutes.

devon: yikes. any commonality for the long ones? are they gptx-chat streaming or long context embeddings?

sam: mostly chat streaming with large system prompts + function calls. The weird part: admission controller labeled them as small (1 GPU slot) so they entered low-priority FIFO lane and then monopolized a worker's KV cache for long sequences.

mira: can you paste the admission log snippet? maybe the estimator is undercounting tokens.

sam: paste below: 
```
[admission] request_id=abc123 model=gpt-large estimated_tokens=512 runtime_est=18s assigned_queue=short
[admission] request_id=def456 model=gpt-large estimated_tokens=48 runtime_est=2s assigned_queue=short
[worker] scheduling request_id=abc123 allocated_gpu=gpu-14 start_ts=1610000
[worker] actual_duration=125s request_id=abc123
```
Looks like estimated_tokens is inconsistent (512 vs actual behavior). The estimator uses `client_token_hint` header + model.max_seq_len, but our code drops system+history tokens when header missing.

linh: infra-bot just posted alert: :warning: admission-saturation us-east-1 high-queue (threshold 200) — triggered at 16:22 UTC.

infra-bot: alert generated: admission_queue_depth=580; p90_wait=94s; gpu_idle_fraction=0.62; affected_pools=[default,interactive].

devon: probable root cause: admission estimator uses client-side hint that some SDKs don't send for streaming calls. For a subset of chat calls we fall back to `model.max_seq_len` incorrectly set to a small value for some model variants — mis-annotation in model catalog. That causes head-of-line where a long job is treated as short and blocks FIFO.

mira: quick mitigations: 1) switch admission to worst-case token cap for chat endpoints (safer) 2) enable preemption for jobs exceeding runtime threshold 3) add short-job priority lane (age-based). Which do we want as hotfix?

ops-oncall: prioritize low-friction: (1) flip flag to use worst-case token cap for chat — we can roll it for us-east-1 only. Also raise admission token refill rate by 20% temporarily.

sam: agree. I'll open a canary PR to change estimator fallback and a separate patch to increase refill rate. PRs: #3287 (estimator fallback), #3290 (refill).

devon: rollback plan? if we see regression (higher tail latency), revert refill first. For estimator, canary to 10% traffic then 100%.

mira: ops-oncall, can you run the one-liner to patch the admission config in cluster? 

ops-oncall: running now: `kubectl -n infra patch configmap admission-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"chat_token_fallback":"worst_case"}}'` -> applied.

deploy-bot: Started rollout of admission-config patch to us-east-1 (canary subset).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout complete. 2/2 canary replicas updated.

sam: patch PR #3287 merged to main, will monitor.

mira: added a temporary metric: `admission_estimator_mismatch_count` and a dashboard panel showing estimated vs actual token ratios.

infra-bot: metric event: estimator_mismatch spike -> reduced by 92% post-canary.

devon: next steps for code fix: update model-catalog import to ensure `model.max_seq_len` is normalized (PR #3295) and add unit tests to prevent truncation. Also add short-job prioritization heuristic for fairness. I'll pick up #3295.

ops-oncall: after patch: queue depth dropped to 48, p90_wait=3.2s, GPU utilization improved to 78% node-avg. Leaving monitoring on for 1h.

sam: thanks all. keeping this thread open until metrics stabilize. If anything spikes, ping @ops-oncall. :thumbsup:

linh: noted — good catch, folks.

mira: follow-up doc coming with recommended scheduler changes (SRF-ish heuristic + preemptible lease).

sam: closing in 2h if stable.
